articles.title: I Researched AI Narration and Music Twice. The Second Pass Changed Two of My Conclusions.
articles.excerpt: I make videos with code and AI tools. Product promos, a music video or two, and lately a series about the history of Xianyang, the old Qin capital. Two thousand three hundred years of history in a thr…
articles.body: I make videos with code and AI tools. Product promos, a music video or two, and lately a series about the history of Xianyang, the old Qin capital. Two thousand three hundred years of history in a three-minute film. Every one of those projects ran into the same wall. The visuals I could handle. The voice kept sounding like a navigation app reading me the news. So I went looking for narration that sounds like a person, and background music I could actually use without a lawyer. Twice, it turns out. I did a full pass over the whole market, prices, licences, local models, the works. Then I ran the research again for one specific project, my own machine, a Ryzen 7 3800X with 32GB of RAM and no GPU worth mentioning. Most of the first pass held up. Two conclusions flipped completely.

articles.body: Shadeform is good at one job: finding a GPU virtual machine across 30+ clouds and launching it from one account, so the right alternative depends on whether you also want someone to finish the run for you. Nodus takes the job itself, runs it on the cheapest capacity that will finish it, and restores its checkpoint if a machine is lost, at $2.60 per NVIDIA H100 SXM hour on the Nodus pricing page . SkyPilot is the open-source choice for your own cloud accounts, Vast.ai has some of the lowest H100 sticker prices, and Runpod suits per-second container pods. We build Nodus, so read with that in mind. Every fact about another company links to its own docs or pricing page, and every sum is written out. What does Shadeform actually do for you? Shadeform is a broker for VMs, not a job runner.

articles.title: POV: You watch your coding agent accidentally write an unhandled exception for the seventh time today
articles.excerpt: POV: You are staring blankly at your monitor while your coding agent loops on a task, frantically adding optional chaining to an async function because it tried to read a property from a null value. T…
articles.body: POV: You are staring blankly at your monitor while your coding agent loops on a task, frantically adding optional chaining to an async function because it tried to read a property from a null value. The agent is caught in the loop it runs over and over. It writes code. It runs code. It reads the error. It tries to fix it. Except the language it is writing allows nulls and implicit exceptions. Every time the schema shifts slightly, the whole thing crashes at runtime. I am Jake Burwick, a high school student. I built Vow, an open source programming language under the MIT license designed specifically for AI agents to write. The source code is public at github.com/JakeBurwick/vow. Vow has no nulls and no exceptions. If a function can fail, it returns a Result value.

articles.title: Design Metaprinciples: Less Art, More Engineering
articles.excerpt: Design Metaprinciples: Less Art, More Engineering Software developers love principles, and for a good reason: principles shape how a design is created. They say what to do, what to avoid and, ideally,…
articles.body: Design Metaprinciples: Less Art, More Engineering Software developers love principles, and for a good reason: principles shape how a design is created. They say what to do, what to avoid and, ideally, why. Metaprinciples sit one level up. They shape how the principles themselves are chosen, and they should answer the same "why?" for the whole set. Below are the five metaprinciples that govern the systems I design. To keep them on the ground, I will explain all five with one ordinary thing: a train. 1. One answer per question, or an explicit refusal Determinism with its honesty clause Nobody at a railway decides how far apart the rails should be. That question was answered once, the answer is called the gauge, and because of it a car built in one country can run on the lines of another.

articles.title: ULA traces Vulcan Centaur rocket failure to 'inadequate fuel supply' to 1st-stage engines
articles.excerpt: United Launch Alliance has traced the Nov. 15 failure of its Vulcan Centaur rocket to an inadequate supply of propellant to the vehicle's first-stage engines.
articles.body: United Launch Alliance (ULA) is getting a handle on why its Vulcan Centaur rocket failed over the weekend. That failure, which occurred during a launch from Florida's Space Coast on Sunday (Nov. 15), led to the loss of 40 Amazon Leo internet satellites . ULA soon traced the anomaly to Vulcan Centaur's first stage , and it has now pinpointed the problem area even further. "While work remains to determine cause, preliminary indications are that the low booster thrust was the result of inadequate fuel supply from the vehicle to the BE-4 engines, not from the performance of the engines," ULA wrote in an update today (Nov. 18). This is good news for Blue Origin , Jeff Bezos' aerospace company, which builds the BE-4.

articles.body: The pace is picking up on building, testing, and plotting out the flight paths for a trio of NASA Ingenuity-class helicopters to investigate Mars after riding there on a nuclear-powered rocket. NASA's Skyfall mission will see those mini-choppers dropped off at Mars by the space agency's Space Reactor-1 Freedom (SR-1) rocket, the first fission nuclear-powered interplanetary spacecraft slated for launch in late 2028. After its cruise phase and initial Mars flyby in 2029, that nuclear carrier craft will make a second Mars approach in the Fall of 2030 to unleash a SkyFall entry capsule outfitted with a fleet of small aerial vehicles that will soar across the Red Planet . But some experts are questioning why NASA is combining two such high-profile missions into one.
